cards.title: Introduction to Flask Request Object
cards.content:
In Flask, the request object is a global proxy that contains all the data sent by the client to the server during an HTTP request.

It allows you to access form data, query parameters, headers, JSON payloads, and uploaded files.

from flask import request

@app.route('/login', methods=['POST'])
def login():
    username = request.form['username']
    return f'Welcome {username}!'

cards.title: Query Parameters vs Form Data
cards.content:
Depending on how the client sends data, you access it differently:

  • Query Parameters: Sent in the URL (e.g., /search?q=flask). Accessed via request.args.get('q').
  • Form Data: Sent via HTML forms using POST. Accessed via request.form.get('username').

cards.title: Handling JSON Data in APIs
cards.content:
When building REST APIs, clients usually send data in JSON format with the Content-Type: application/json header.

You can easily parse this data using request.get_json() or the shorthand request.json.

@app.route('/api/data', methods=['POST'])
def receive_data():
    content = request.get_json()
    name = content.get('name')
    return {"status": "success", "received": name}, 201

cards.title: Match Request Attributes to Their Use Case

steps: Client sends an HTTP request to the Flask server
Flask routes the URL to the matching view function
The view function accesses data using the global request object
The view function returns a response object or string
Flask sends the HTTP response back to the client

cards.title: Handling File Uploads
cards.content:
Files sent via a multipart HTML form can be accessed using request.files.

@app.route('/upload', methods=['POST'])
def upload_file():
    file = request.files['file']
    file.save(f"/var/www/uploads/{file.filename}")
    return 'File uploaded successfully!'

options.text: Files must be sent via JSON payloads
GET method must be used for file uploads

cards.title: Summary of Flask Requests
cards.content:
You have learned how to handle various types of client input in Flask:

  • request.args for query parameters
  • request.form for form submissions
  • request.json for API payloads
  • request.files for file uploads

Mastering these tools enables you to build robust web applications and APIs.
